Interface InterceptionTarget

public interface InterceptionTarget
The bean an interceptor instance was created for.

An interceptor that no scope holds, a @Prototype or one with no scope, is created by the container for one intercepted bean and destroyed with it. Such an interceptor can inject this type, in its constructor or any other injection point of its own, to learn which bean that is: the definition of the bean being created, or, for a proxy that resolves its interceptors for each target, the definition of the target. The definition carries the qualifier of the bean, so two beans of one class, for example two beans of one @EachBean, are told apart.

It is only available while the container creates an interceptor for an intercepted bean. Injecting it into any other bean, into a dependency of the interceptor, or into an interceptor obtained by a plain lookup fails with a NoSuchBeanException; a @Nullable injection point receives null instead. A singleton interceptor, or one of a custom scope, is shared by many beans and never receives it.

Since:
5.3.0
